To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) ethnicity and race are socially constructed; (2) they are constructed by individuals and groups in specific historical and cultural contexts and in response to specific agendas; (3) their construction depends on both the context in which it occurs and the resources that individuals and groups have available for constructing identities; and (4) the construction of ethnicity and race is a dynamic, ongoing process.
